Lessons.Title: Use a Protractor to Draw Angles
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will use a protractor to draw angles of given measurements.
In earlier lessons, you reasoned about angle measurements, learned to use a protractor, and measured given angles. You have sketched angles by referring to clock faces and sketched estimates of angles of a given size based on benchmark angles. In this lesson, you use a protractor to draw angles of specified measurements (not limited to benchmark angles) and to verify the size of angles in your peers’ drawings.

2021 lesson activities: Warm-up: Estimation Exploration: Long Hand and Short Hand (10 minutes); Activity 1: Draw These Angles (15 minutes); Activity 2: Angles Made to Order (20 minutes); Cool-down: A Ray or Two (5 minutes)
Corrected mathematical focus: Use the protractor vertex, zero baseline and desired degree mark to construct a ray at a specified turn.

Edulytics authored guidance: Draw a baseline ray and mark its endpoint as the vertex. Set the protractor centre at the endpoint and align the baseline with 0°. Mark the target degree and draw a second ray through the mark; verify with measurement.
First-party Cool-down (not publisher assessment): Use a protractor to draw a 75° angle and label the vertex.
Images, drawing/protractor accuracy, partner tasks and the gated original publisher Cool-down require original task evidence and teacher/visual review.
